newsitem.title: CROATIA: Tudjman's health better after reported cancer bout.
newsitem.headline: Tudjman's health better after reported cancer bout.

text.p: President Franjo Tudjman of Croatia, said by Western diplomats to have been stricken by cancer last year, has returned to good health after treatment, state radio said on Friday.

With key elections pending, ruling party strategists have tried to show that Tudjman, 74, is fit and the report by his personal medical council quoted by the radio was clearly intended to bolster that impression.

Tudjman was treated at a U.S. military hospital late last year for what diplomats said was stomach cancer that might prove terminal. He returned home looking weak and gaunt but his appearance has since improved markedly.
The Croatian government and state-dominated media have said only that Tudjman had suffered from unspecified stomach ailments and swollen lymph nodes.
"President Tudjman underwent his regular medical checkup on Friday during which it was stated that the results of his treatment were exceptionally favourable," state radio said.

"His stomach problems have receded and his weight is back to normal. The swelling of lymph nodes continues to go down. All test results are normal. The president has full working abilities, without restrictions."
It added that the medical council would continue to monitor Tudjman's treatment "in cooperation with foreign doctors." It did not specify the treatment.

Tudjman's once luxuriant mane of silver hair has thinned dramatically since November. But the former communist general turned conservative nationalist has recovered much of his old vigour, moving about briskly and delivering long and robust speeches.
Croatia holds elections for regional and municipal governments on April 13 and Tudjman's HDZ party will be hardpressed to beat a rising opposition alliance in some key urban districts.

Tudjman, who led Croatia to independence from Yugoslavia in 1991 and retains great charisma at home despite a decline in his party's popularity, plans to seek re-election later in the year and is likely to win easily.
